## `scripts/fp/posters/poster_art.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Poster palettes and the procedural fallback art (slice D): a soft two-tone gradient in the colours of the poster's kind (or its mayor), so a poster is never blank offline or while its image is on the way. Static and deterministic from the cache key.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `PALETTES = { "campaign": [Color(0.09, 0.11, 0.2), Color(0.32, 0.38, 0.55), Color(1.0, 0.72, 0.0)],...`: Base colours per poster family: [deep, light, accent].

### Functions

- `static func family(kind: String) -> String`: The poster family of a kind or pool name: "campaign_argon" -> "campaign".
- `static func palette(kind: String) -> Array`: [deep, light, accent] for a kind or pool; campaigns of a mayor use the mayor's colour.
- `static func mayor_index(id: String) -> int`: Index of the mayor with this id ("argon"), or -1.
- `static func procedural(kind: String, key: String) -> Texture2D`: A gradient texture for a poster of this kind; the angle and stops vary with the key.

## `scripts/fp/posters/poster_compositor.gd`

extends `Node`

Draws poster text over poster images (slice D): a one-shot SubViewport (update mode ONCE) holds the image and the layout's panels and Labels (Lilita One for display type, system serif and sans for newspaper and body copy), the result is read back asynchronously (RenderingDevice texture_get_data_async, so the main thread never stalls on the GPU), mipmapped and VRAM-compressed on a background thread and wrapped in an ImageTexture. One job renders at a time, nearest first. Headless runs skip the drawing and return the raw image, so tests check the pipeline and not the pixels of the text.

### Signals

- `composited(job_id: String, tex: Texture2D)`

### Constants

- `FONT_PATH = "res://fonts/lilita_one_regular.ttf"`
- `WORKER = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_worker.gd")`
- `SERIF = ["DejaVu Serif", "Georgia", "Times New Roman", "Liberation Serif", "Noto Serif", "serif"]`
- `FRAMES_BETWEEN_JOBS = 2`: Idle frames between two jobs, so a burst of composites never stacks readback stalls.
- `SANS = ["Fira Sans", "Source Sans Pro", "DejaVu Sans", "Arial", "Liberation Sans", "Noto Sans"...`

### Properties

- `done_count: int`: Jobs finished so far (tests).
- `max_main_ms: float`: Longest main-thread cost of one composite (readback, or texture creation), in ms.
- `max_read_ms: float`: The same split: the readback request (or blocking read) and the texture upload, in ms.

### Inner classes

- `Mailbox`: Thread-safe drop box for readback bytes (see _mail).

### Functions

- `func enqueue(job_id: String, base: Texture2D, elements: Array, px: Vector2i, order: float = 0.0) -> void`: Queues a composite of base under elements at px; composited(job_id, tex) follows (deferred, immediately with base when headless). order sorts the queue (smaller first, e.g. distance).
- `func cancel(job_id: String) -> void`: Drops a queued job (a running one still finishes; listeners ignore stale ids).
- `func pending(job_id: String) -> bool`: True while job_id waits or renders.
- `func queued() -> int`
- `static func fit(font: Font, s: String, box: Vector2, max_px: float, lines: int, line_spacing: float = 0.0) -> int`: The largest font size <= max_px at which s wraps into at most `lines` lines inside box, with no word wider than the box (line_spacing is a fraction of the size).

## `scripts/fp/posters/poster_director.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Decides what each poster carrier shows (slice D): mayors' campaigns on billboards in their own districts, the GridFall Gazette at bus shelters, shop ads named after the real businesses, "Coming soon" hoardings on construction sites, ordinance and incident notices on homes and workshops, protest flyers after a district protest, and lease boards. Every image prompt comes from assets/posters/prompts.json plus SimDefs and directory data (never raw LLM text except the de-branded slogan or headline); every overlay string goes through SimDefs.debrand(). An assignment is {"key", "kind" (pool), "family", "prompt", "size", "priority", "overlay"}.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `PROMPTS_PATH = "res://assets/posters/prompts.json"`
- `WIDE = "1536x640"`
- `TALL = "768x1152"`
- `SLOGAN_MAX = 60`
- `CAMPAIGN_REFRESH_DAYS = 3`
- `CAMPAIGN_MOOD_SHIFT = 1.0`
- `INCIDENT_RADIUS = 6.0`: Walls within this many tiles of an active incident show its warning.
- `AD_POOL = { "cafe": "ad_cafe", "diner": "ad_cafe", "deli": "ad_cafe", "noodle bar": "ad_cafe", "b...`: business_kind() (lower case) -> pre-baked ad pool; anything else is ad_default.
- `TAGLINES = { "cafe": "Fresh coffee from 7 am", "diner": "Breakfast all day", "deli": "Sandwiches m...`: Shop copy by business kind (falls back to the pool line).
- `POOL_TAGLINES = { "ad_cafe": "Good food, good company", "ad_bakery": "Baked fresh every morning", "ad_m...`
- `DEFAULT_SLOGANS = { "argon": "Power, water and parks that just work.", "deepseek": "Smarter roads. Faster...`: Slogans a mayor runs on before their first public post.
- `ORDINANCE_LINES = { "public_transit": "New bus and tram routes for every district. Expect up to 30% less ...`: Plain-language effect lines for ordinance notices.
- `COMPLAINT_LINES = { "power": "Keep the lights on!", "water": "Clean water now!", "sewage": "Fix the sewer...`: Protest complaint -> placard line.
- `POWER_EVENTS = ["blackout", "power_line"]`
- `WATER_EVENTS = ["water_main", "flood", "sewage_burst"]`

### Properties

- `campaigns: Array[Dictionary]`: Per mayor: {} until a campaign exists, else {"key", "kind", "family", "prompt", "size", "priority", "overlay", "day", "mood", "word", "variant", "from_post"}.
- `gazette: Dictionary`: The current Gazette assignment ({} before the first paper).

### Functions

- `func setup(p_ctx: FpContext) -> void`
- `func prompt(body: String) -> String`: The full image prompt for a body: body + " " + the style lock (same string the generator uses).
- `func seed_from_brain() -> void`: Seeds the Gazette from brain.last_paper and every mayor's campaign (their latest post, else a default slogan), so posters do not wait a game day for the next signal. Existing state is kept.
- `func on_mayor_decided(mi: int, entry: Dictionary) -> bool`: A mayor decided (CityBrain.mayor_decided). Refreshes that mayor's campaign at most every CAMPAIGN_REFRESH_DAYS game days, when the district's mood moved by CAMPAIGN_MOOD_SHIFT or the mayor's mood word changed; the first real post always replaces the default slogan. Returns true when the campaign changed.
- `func on_news(paper: Dictionary) -> bool`: The Gazette published a paper (CityBrain.news_published). Returns true when it changed.
- `static func gazette_topic(paper: Dictionary) -> String`: Topic of a paper for the offline photo: crews, construction, park or skyline.
- `static func slogan_of(post: String) -> String`: The first <= 60 characters of a post, cut at a word boundary, de-branded.
- `func assign(slot: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: The assignment for a slot ({"id", "tile", "carrier", ...}); {} when it should show nothing.
- `func gazette_or_default() -> Dictionary`: The current Gazette, or a front page built from the city's own numbers before the first paper.
- `func ad_for(i: int, size: String = WIDE) -> Dictionary`: An ad for the business on tile i (or a district ad when it has none), as the pre-baked pool image.
- `func ordinance_notice(key: String) -> Dictionary`: A notice for an enacted ordinance.
- `func incident_near(i: int) -> Dictionary`: A warning for the nearest active incident within INCIDENT_RADIUS of tile i, or {}.
- `func incident_notice(ev: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: The warning poster for an incident event (procedural layout over the pre-baked notice photo).
- `func placard(d: int) -> Dictionary`: A protest flyer when district d protested yesterday, else {}.
- `func hoarding(i: int) -> Dictionary`: "Coming soon" for the construction site on tile i ({} when there is none or it is a road job).
- `func slot_hash(slot_id: String) -> int`: Deterministic per-slot hash seeded by the city.
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`: Campaign state for the save: campaign_day, campaign_mood and the assignments themselves.
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`

## `scripts/fp/posters/poster_feature.gd`

extends `FpFeature`

Campaign, newspaper, shop and notice posters on the streets (slice D). Wires the HY image client (GmiImageClient), the director (what each carrier shows), the surfaces (carriers and poster faces on tile holders) and the compositor (crisp text drawn over the image). Posters within VIS_PROP of the player get a composite with their text (at most MAX_COMPOSITES); farther ones show the shared image of their key. Billboards and shelter lightboxes glow at night. E on a poster opens a full-screen viewer. Offline (every gate) all art comes from the pre-baked set.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `DIRECTOR = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_director.gd")`
- `SURFACES = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_surfaces.gd")`
- `COMPOSITOR = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_compositor.gd")`
- `LAYOUTS = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_layouts.gd")`
- `ART = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_art.gd")`
- `MAX_COMPOSITES = 32`
- `UPDATE_S = 0.5`: Night glow and composite upkeep run at 2 Hz.
- `MODAL = &"poster"`
- `NIGHT_BILLBOARD = 0.9`: Emission energies (see glow()): billboards are lamp-lit at night only; shelter lightboxes are backlit, faint by day and brightest at night. Measured against the night exposure: above about 1.6 the white of a print blooms and its text loses contrast.
- `DAY_SHELTER = 0.3`
- `NIGHT_SHELTER = 1.3`
- `OWNER = "posters"`

### Properties

- `max_composites: int`: Composite cap (MAX_COMPOSITES; tests lower it).
- `slots: Dictionary`: slot id -> slot (poster_surfaces.gd).
- `assigned: Dictionary`: slot id -> assignment (poster_director.gd).
- `base_tex: Dictionary`: key -> the poster image (pre-baked, cached, live or procedural).
- `composites: Dictionary`: composite id -> {"tex": Texture2D or null while rendering, "slots": {slot id: true}, "key"}.

### Functions

- `func feature_id() -> String`
- `func setup(p_ctx: FpContext) -> void`
- `func on_world_rebuilt() -> void`
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`
- `func teardown() -> void`
- `func glow(kind: String = "billboard")`: Emission energy of a lit poster from view.night (0 noon .. 1 midnight). The emission is the print itself (EMISSION_OP_MULTIPLY), so this is how bright the print glows on its own.
- `func update_composites() -> void`: Gives slots within VIS_PROP of the player a composite (nearest first, at most MAX_COMPOSITES distinct ones) and releases the composite of slots beyond 1.25 * VIS_PROP. When the cap is reached, the composites of the farthest slots make room for nearer ones.
- `func on_mayor_decided(mi: int, entry: Dictionary) -> void`: CityBrain.mayor_decided: refreshes the mayor's campaign on every billboard and wall showing it.
- `func on_news(paper: Dictionary) -> void`: CityBrain.news_published: a new Gazette front page at every shelter.
- `func pick(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, max_dist: float) -> Dictionary`: Ray against the poster faces within max_dist: the nearest front-facing hit.
- `func target_for(id: String, p: Vector3, dist: float) -> Dictionary`: The interaction target of slot id (S0 §9 target dict).
- `static func title_of(a: Dictionary) -> String`: A short human title for an assignment ("Ada Okafor's campaign poster").
- `func open_viewer(id: String) -> void`: Full-screen view of a poster in the HUD's overlay slot (modal "poster"; E or Esc closes it).
- `func close_viewer() -> void`
- `func viewer_open() -> bool`: True while the full-screen viewer is open.
- `func self_test() -> Dictionary`
- `func photo_shots() -> Array`: "billboard" (the billboard nearest City Hall, framed at 6 m), "bus_shelter" and the billboard again at night, all eye-level.

## `scripts/fp/posters/poster_surfaces.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Finds poster carriers on CityView's tile holders and gives each one poster faces (slice D). Precedence on a carrier: H's Poster_<n> meshes, then a G1 `poster_slot` meta, then a quad at the measured panel of the legacy model. Carriers: billboards, bus shelters (both faces of the gf stop's ad panel), wall posters on lots (H's PosterSpot_<n>, else the baked flat-wall and storefront-window spots of assets/posters/wall_spots.json, else the wall box face), hoardings on construction sites and lease boards. Every node added under a holder carries meta fp_owner = "posters" and dies with the holder. A slot is {"id": "<tile>:<carrier>:<n>", "tile", "carrier", "faces": [face], "size": Vector2 (world units), "pos", "normal", "lit", "nodes": [Node], "spot": {...} (walls)}; a face is {"mesh": MeshInstance3D, "center", "right", "up", "normal", "half": Vector2} in world space.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `OWNER = "posters"`
- `REAL_BILLBOARD = "res://models/real/props/billboard.glb"`
- `GF_STOP = "res://models/props/bus_stop.glb"`
- `REAL_STOP = "res://models/real/props/bus_stop.glb"`
- `SPOTS_PATH = "res://assets/posters/wall_spots.json"`
- `BILLBOARD_SIZE = Vector2(0.34, 0.15)`: The legacy billboard's sign face: 0.34 x 0.15 at y 0.20-0.35, front plane z 0.0045.
- `BILLBOARD_XF = Transform3D(Basis(), Vector3(0, 0.275, 0.006))`
- `GF_STOP_SIZE = Vector2(0.08, 0.09)`: The gf stop's gf_ad_pink lightbox (x 0.06-0.14, y 0.045-0.135) sits behind its opaque back wall (gf_sky_blue, z -0.058 to -0.052) and pokes out of the back to z -0.060: the poster faces the road just in front of the wall's inner face and the sidewalk just behind the box.
- `GF_STOP_FRONT = Transform3D(Basis(), Vector3(0.10, 0.09, -0.0515))`
- `GF_STOP_BACK = Transform3D(Basis(Vector3.UP, PI), Vector3(0.10, 0.09, -0.0605))`
- `REAL_STOP_SIZE = Vector2(0.063, 0.106)`: The real stop's lightbox at its west end (x -0.123), facing -X.
- `REAL_STOP_XF = Transform3D(Basis(Vector3.UP, -PI * 0.5), Vector3(-0.1245, 0.065, 0.0))`
- `WALL_OFFSET = 0.002`: Wall posters sit this far off the wall (4 cm), window posters off the glass.
- `WINDOW_OFFSET = 0.0012`
- `WALL_FALLBACK_SIZE = Vector2(0.06, 0.09)`: The contract's fallback wall poster (1.2 x 1.8 m) centred 0.07 above LOT_TOP.
- `WALL_FALLBACK_Y = WS.LOT_TOP + 0.07`
- `FENCE_H = 0.05`: The S0 construction kit's fence (construction_kit.gd _fence): 1 m tall at +-0.47, 8 mm thick.

- `SIDES = {"+z": Vector3(0, 0, 1), "-z": Vector3(0, 0, -1), "+x": Vector3(1, 0, 0), "-x": Vector3...`
- `WALL_PREFIXES = ["Brick", "Siding", "Stone", "Plaster", "Concrete_Wall", "Concrete_Panel", "Panel"]`

### Properties

- `spots: Dictionary`: Baked wall spots by model path (see wall_spot_baker.gd).

- `func wall_lot(i: int) -> bool`: True when lot i carries a wall poster (deterministic per city seed).

## `scripts/fp/posters/poster_worker.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

One background thread that runs poster image jobs in order (slice D): decode, resize, WebP, mipmaps and VRAM compression. A plain Thread rather than WorkerThreadPool tasks: Image.compress may fan out onto the pool and wait for it, which can starve when the caller is itself a pool task. Jobs touch only their own input dictionary; the main thread collects finished inputs with take_done().

### Functions

- `static func finish_image(input: Dictionary) -> void`: Job for composites: opaque RGB, mipmaps and block compression of input.image (or of the raw RGBA8 readback input.data at input.px); sets input.ok.
- `func push(fn: Callable, input: Dictionary) -> void`: Queues fn.call(input) on the thread.
- `func take_done() -> Array`: Inputs whose job finished since the last call, in order.
- `func pending() -> int`: Jobs queued or running.
- `func stop() -> void`: Drops queued jobs, lets a running one finish and joins the thread.

## `scripts/fp/posters/wall_spot_baker.gd`

extends `SceneTree`

Offline bake of wall-poster spots (slice D). For every zone building model and each of its four sides it finds the wall plane (the depth most wall-material rays hit near the wall box face) and, on that plane, the largest standard poster (6-sheet 1.2 x 1.8 m, 4-sheet 1.0 x 1.5 m, A0 0.84 x 1.19 m) that sits on flat wall nearest a corner: every ray of a grid over the poster must first hit outward-facing wall material on the plane, so no window, door, trim, sign or awning is covered and nothing floats. Writes res://assets/posters/wall_spots.json: {model path: {"box": [x, y, z, sx, sy, sz], "spots": {side: {"p": [x, cy, z], "size": [w, h]}}}} side is +z, -z, +x or -x (the outward normal in model space); p.x/p.z lie on the wall plane in model space, cy is the world height of the poster centre (independent of the building scale) and size is in world units. The checks cover building scales 0.9 (S0) to 1.0 (G1). Run: godot --headless --path . -s scripts/fp/posters/wall_spot_baker.gd

### Constants

- `OUT = "res://assets/posters/wall_spots.json"`
- `DIRS = ["res://models/real/zones/"]`
- `WALL_PREFIXES = ["Brick", "Siding", "Stone", "Plaster", "Concrete_Wall", "Concrete_Panel", "Panel"]`
- `GLASS_PREFIXES = ["Glass_Shop"]`
- `SKIP_PREFIXES = ["Grass", "Sidewalk", "Dirt", "Concrete_Floor", "Hedge", "Leaves", "Bark"]`
- `MIN_WALL_H = 0.03`: Surfaces shorter than this (plinths, sills) do not define the wall box.
- `SIZES = [Vector2(0.06, 0.09), Vector2(0.05, 0.075), Vector2(0.042, 0.0595)]`: Poster sizes in world units, largest first, and centre heights (world y), preferred first.
- `HEIGHTS = [0.074, 0.08, 0.068]`
- `WINDOW_SIZES = [Vector2(0.042, 0.0595), Vector2(0.03, 0.042)]`: Window posters: A0 and A1, centred about 1.5 m up.
- `WINDOW_HEIGHTS = [0.076, 0.07, 0.082]`
- `MIN_SCALE = 0.9`
- `PLANE_RANGE = 0.08`: The wall plane is searched this far behind the box face.
- `BEHIND_TOL = 0.002`: Hits must lie within these distances behind / in front of the plane (model units).
- `FRONT_TOL = 0.0012`
- `STEP = 0.006`
- `GRID = Vector2i(6, 8)`
- `MARGIN = 0.006`

### Functions

- `func bake(path: String) -> Dictionary`
- `static func frame(box: AABB, side: String) -> Array`: Face frame of a side: [outward normal, horizontal axis u, box face offset along the normal, u range of the box].
